text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic said the election of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as Yugoslav president is the expression of the will of the majority of Yugoslavs.
- Poland will support Yugoslavia's efforts to be fully reintegrated into the international community, Polish officials tell Yugoslav parliamentary delegation on visit to Warsaw.
- Yugoslav-Macedonian expert teams to discuss in Skopje outstanding issues in the implementation of interstate economic and trade agreements.
- Yugoslav Securities Commission approved first issue of 160 million German marks worth of hard currency short-term bonds for road construction in Serbia.
- Industrial output in the first six months this year was 7.6 percent up on the same period last year, according to the Federal Statistics Office.
- Serbia's construction works abroad in 1996 and January-April 1997 were worth a total of $243.2 million, according to the National Bank of Yugoslavia.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic was blocked by police from entering his offices in the Democratic Party of Socialists seat. The DPS main board replaced Bulatovic as party president last week.

- During a talk show on the local television station BK-TV lawyer Nikola Barovic poured water on Serbian Radical Party (SRS) leader Vojislav Seselj after a heated discussion over eviction of a Croat family from their flat in Zemun and was later beaten up by Seselj's bodyguard.
NASA BORBA

- The national movement for the liberation of Kosovo announced new actions to achieve "legitimate aspirations of the Albanian people to live dignified and united in one state," Italian news agency reported from Tirana.

- Serbian presidential and republican elections to be held on September 21, according to the paper's source in ruling party leadership. It says former Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic will be the ruling coalition's presidential candidate.

- Federal parliament session at which Milosevic was elected new Yugoslav president was not convened in advance as regulations require and is therefore illegal, according to constitutional law experts.

- Democratic Party and Serbian Renewal Movement leaders Zoran Djindjic and Vuk Draskovic to speak in front of the City Hall on Thursday night when the two-headed eagle is to be mounted on the building roof.
- Novi Pazar public prosecutor called Sulejman Ugljanin, the president of the Moslem National Council for Sandzak, for an interrogation.
- Yugoslavia's trade deficit could reach three billion dollars this year, says Foreign Trade Institute.
- Yugoslav-Albanian border crossing Vermica near Prizren was reopened after a four-month closure.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Belgrade police detained German television ARD chief correspondent Friedhelm Baebeck for "making too much noise" in a restaurant in central Belgrade.
BORBA

- "The Socialist Party of Serbia has showed it is the strongest party on our political scene, has the best programme and is the best organised," said Serbian Parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic on occasion of the SPS seventh anniversary.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) local branch of Niksic extended its support to the DPS Main Board while the local branches of Andrijevica, Plav and Berane withdrew their support to the main board decisions.
- The DPS Main Board appointed Mihajlo Banjevic, the director of the Montenegrin pension fund, as the new head of the Podgorica DPS branch.

- Maximum annual production capacity of the construction machine factory Radoje Dakic from Podgorica is 500 machines while the minimum cost effective production is 125 machines, according to a special report of experts appointed by the Montenegrin government.
